statement_pretty:
∀ {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y),
  Function.Injective ⇑f → IsClosedMap ⇑f → StableUnderSpecialization (Set.range ⇑f)

referees.justification: Calibrated zero-token rubric evaluation assigns an expected importance of 5.72/10 (confidence 0.26) and classifies the result as a Proposition (p = 0.43) in MSC 14-XX. Independent probability estimates yield P(surprising) = 0.22 and P(a human mathematician cares) = 0.52.

While formally stated for morphisms of schemes, this result is an immediate consequence of the elementary topological fact that the image of a closed map is closed and therefore stable under specialization. The hypothesis of injectivity, as well as the entire scheme-theoretic apparatus, is entirely superfluous, rendering the proposition a needlessly baroque reformulation of a triviality.

editorial.title: Proposition on Specialization Stability of Injective Closed Scheme Morphisms

editorial.unverified_gloss: For any morphism of schemes f : X ⟶ Y whose underlying map of topological spaces is injective and closed, the image of f in Y is stable under specialization. In fact, both the scheme structure and the injectivity hypothesis are redundant: the image of any closed map between topological spaces is closed, and every closed subset is automatically stable under specialization.
